axes.model_access:
It calls no model itself; it is an interface implementation called by clients.
**This server produces no intelligence, only structure** —
what it constrains is how the Agent calls it (step-by-step thinking with revisions allowed);
the actual reasoning is still done by the model behind the client.
axes.runtime: A local Node.js process communicating over stdio. No file or network access needed.
axes.local_files: **No file-access capability whatsoever.** It provides no read/write tools — one of the narrowest-permission entries in this section.
axes.background: Not supported. A pure-computation tool: stateless, no background needed.
axes.tools:
**A single tool** `sequential_thinking`,

whose parameters include:

- thought
- thoughtNumber
- totalThoughts
- nextThoughtNeeded

plus revision (isRevision / revisesThought) and
branching (branchFromThought / branchId) controls.

Output is a structured object.
axes.context:
No cross-session memory. Each call receives the full thinking text;
revisions and branches are passed explicitly via parameters, with no reliance on server-side storage.
axes.permissions:
**No permission risk at all**: no file access, no network access, writes no state.
Its entire permission set is "being able to call one pure function".
axes.fit:
Lets an Agent advance complex problems in a structured, revisable, branchable way.
Not a fit for simple tasks (extra call rounds bring no benefit).

mcp.transport:
stdio only. npx / Docker local process (full README verification 2026-10-08);
there is no official launch method for a remote transport. The Docker image is mcp/sequentialthinking.
mcp.auth:
No separate authentication layer, but **this is the only server in this section with no substantive permission boundary** —
no files, no network, no state; whether auth exists makes no security difference.
mcp.scope:
**No file or network access; reads and writes no external resources.**
Its permission scope is empty — the lowest permission-risk class among MCP servers.
Safe to use in sensitive environments.

sections.工具设计:
**There is only one tool**; its parameters fall into four groups:

| Group | Parameters | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Progress** | `thought` `thoughtNumber` `totalThoughts` `nextThoughtNeeded` | what this step is, how many steps total, whether to continue |
| **Revision** | `isRevision` `revisesThought` | acknowledge revising an earlier step |
| **Branching** | `branchFromThought` `branchId` | fork another reasoning path from some step |
| **Extension** | `needsMoreThoughts` | discover mid-way that more steps are needed |

**"Revision" and "branching" are this server's core value** —
they let the Agent go back and change steps mid-reasoning, instead of one path to the end.
sections.关键澄清：它不提升模型能力:
This is the most easily misunderstood point.

```
This server calls no model and does no reasoning.
It constrains how the client calls it; reasoning is still done by the model.
```

**It solves a "structure" problem, not an "intelligence" problem**:

| What it does | What it does not do |
|---|---|
| Makes reasoning visible step by step | Make the model smarter |
| Allows mid-way revision | Improve conclusion accuracy |
| Supports parallel branch exploration | Reduce token consumption (it increases it instead) |
| Lets the caller observe the process | Replace thinking-budget control |

**Using it on simple tasks adds call rounds with no benefit.** The applicable scenarios the README itself lists are also limited to:
breaking down complex problems, analyses that may need correction, tasks with unclear initial scope, long tasks needing irrelevant information filtered out.
sections.权限评价:
**The lowest permission-risk class among MCP servers**; safe in sensitive environments:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Read files | ❌ none |
| Write files | ❌ none |
| Network access | ❌ none |
| Persisted state | ❌ none |
| Delete capability | ❌ none |

Its entire permission set is "being able to call one pure function". This class of server deserves calling out —
it shows the MCP ecosystem also has zero-risk tools; not everything is permission-sensitive.
